title: Networking Basics
description: Essential computer networking protocols, architectures, and addressing fundamentals.

cards.title: OSI 7-Layer Model
cards.summary: Conceptual framework partitioning network communications into seven distinct abstraction layers.
cards.mnemonic: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away (Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application)
acceptedAnswers: The OSI model has 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
A 7-layer framework describing network protocols from physical hardware signals up to end-user applications.
cards.hint: Think of the mnemonic: 'Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away'.

cards.title: TCP 3-Way Handshake
cards.summary: Method used by TCP to establish a reliable full-duplex connection between client and server.
cards.mnemonic: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK — Say Hello, Say Hello Back, Acknowledge Connection
acceptedAnswers: The client sends SYN, the server responds with SYN-ACK, and the client replies with ACK to establish a connection.
A three-step handshake: SYN packet from client, SYN-ACK from server, ACK packet from client.
cards.hint: Three packet steps: client starts with SYN, server responds with both, client finishes with ACK.

cards.title: DNS Resolution Hierarchy
cards.summary: Hierarchical decentralized naming system translating human-friendly domain names to IP addresses.
cards.mnemonic: Root to TLD to Authoritative: Root tree branches down to specific dot-coms to authoritative host records.
acceptedAnswers: A recursive resolver queries the Root server, then the TLD server, and finally the Authoritative name server for the IP address.
DNS translates domain names into numerical IP addresses through root, top-level domain, and authoritative servers.
cards.hint: Hierarchical lookup steps: Recursive resolver -> Root -> TLD (.com) -> Authoritative server.

cards.title: NAT Traversal (STUN/TURN/ICE)
cards.summary: Techniques allowing peer-to-peer communication across Network Address Translation (NAT) gateways and firewalls.
cards.mnemonic: STUN Sees you, TURN Relays you, ICE Chooses the path
acceptedAnswers: STUN discovers public IP/ports, TURN acts as a fallback relay server, and ICE coordinates candidate path selection.
NAT traversal uses STUN for discovery, TURN for relay fallback, and ICE to negotiate the best media path.
cards.hint: STUN discovers public endpoint, TURN acts as relay fallback, ICE coordinates candidate selection.

cards.title: Subnet Mask & CIDR
cards.summary: Bitmask separating IP addresses into network prefix bits and host identifier bits.
cards.mnemonic: Mask covers the network, leftover bits name the hosts (e.g. /24 leaves 8 host bits for 254 hosts).
acceptedAnswers: A 32-bit number performing bitwise AND with an IP address to isolate network ID from host ID, denoted by slash notation.
Subnet masking divides an IP network into subnetworks using prefix length notation such as /24.
cards.hint: Bitwise mask separating network prefix from host bits, commonly expressed in CIDR slash notation.
